title: Myelofibrosis as a disease of chronic intrinsic stress: a three-loop model of disease evolution
task: Explain myelofibrosis evolution through chronic intrinsic stress and senescence
key_results: Three-loop model integrating oncogenic stress → senescence → fibrotic microenvironment and blast transformation; senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) with IL-1 family cytokines identified as link between cellular stress and tissue pathology
comments: Primarily a theoretical framework proposing senescence as central mechanism; predictions remain largely untested experimentally despite mechanistic plausibility.

model_io.model: Three-loop disease evolution framework for myelofibrosis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Persistent oncogenic signaling imposes multiple cellular stresses leading to senescence
hypotheses.result: Senescence creates heterogeneous cellular states (arrested, inflammatory, stress-tolerant) across MF ecosystem

hypotheses.hypothesis: Senescence-associated inflammation drives stromal remodeling and fibrosis
hypotheses.result: SASP cytokines establish persistent fibrotic microenvironment through structural loop

hypotheses.hypothesis: Epigenetic erosion and developmental plasticity enable escape from senescence pressure
hypotheses.result: Escape loop facilitates blast-phase transformation

title: Mathematical modelling of malaria-HIV/AIDS-tuberculosis triple co-infection: dynamics, bifurcation, and Sub-Saharan African data calibration
task: Mathematical modeling of malaria-HIV/AIDS-TB triple co-infection with bifurcation analysis and regional calibration
key_results: R₀=2.27 (HIV 2.27, TB 2.17, malaria 0.96); malaria invasion number in HIV-TB endemic state is 1.80; integrated co-infection treatment reduces 20-year infectious burden 5.6 pp more than disease-specific treatment
comments: Sophisticated 37-compartment model with rigorous next-generation matrix derivation; backward bifurcation absent at calibrated parameters limits prediction of complex dynamics.

inputs: co-infection prevalence data from Nigeria, Tanzania, Cameroon, Uganda
transmission rates (vector-borne malaria, sexual HIV, respiratory TB)
treatment parameters for single and multiple infections
outputs: basic reproduction number R₀ and component Rᵢ

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cross-disease susceptibility enhancement does not alter bifurcation direction at R₀ threshold
hypotheses.result: Centre-manifold analysis confirms forward bifurcation regardless of cross-disease effects at calibrated parameters

hypotheses.hypothesis: Basic reproduction number is the maximum of disease-specific R values in multi-pathogen setting
hypotheses.result: R₀=max(Rₘₐₗₐᵣᵢₐ=0.96, Rₕᵢᵥ=2.27, R_ₜᵦ=2.17)=2.27; malaria persists via invasion number 1.80

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integrated co-infection treatment yields greater burden reduction than disease-specific approaches
hypotheses.result: 5.6 percentage point additional reduction in 20-year infectious burden

title: Fractional-order insights into multistable calcium signaling in dementia-affected neuroglial networks
task: Fractional-order modeling of amyloid-beta-induced calcium dysregulation in astrocytes with multistability analysis
key_results: Fractional-order framework reproduces silent states, rhythmic spiking, and mixed-amplitude oscillations; period-n oscillations identified via bifurcation; multistability and synchronization revealed across coupled astrocyte populations
comments: Novel application of fractional calculus to neuroglial calcium dynamics; lack of experimental validation limits claims about amyloid-beta mechanistic insights.

model_io.model: Bifurcation analysis (Λβ and Iₑₓₜ as parameters)
Coupled astrocytic network via IP₃ gap junction exchange

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fractional-order derivatives capture memory effects in astrocytic calcium signaling
hypotheses.result: Modified Atangana–Baleanu–Caputo framework reproduces experimentally observed dynamical regimes including multistability

hypotheses.hypothesis: Amyloid-beta modulates calcium oscillation amplitude and frequency via bifurcation
hypotheses.result: Bifurcation analysis shows Λβ concentration controls transitions between dynamical states; period-n oscillations with nested limit cycles observed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Intercellular coupling and fractional orders jointly regulate astrocyte synchronization
hypotheses.result: Coupled populations exhibit multistability and synchronization dependent on coupling strength and fractional order heterogeneity

title: Exploring complete blood count (CBC) data patterns for early detection of hematological disorders using machine learning
task: Machine learning classification of hematological disorders from complete blood count data
key_results: 90.1–90.3% accuracy and 0.839–0.842 MCC for 22-class classification; red cell distribution width, platelet count, and RBC count most influential; poor performance on rare conditions (CHIP F1=0.14, hemophilia/von Willebrand F1=0.35–0.37)
comments: Strong aggregate performance masks severe class imbalance issues; SMOTE applied only to training data appropriately prevents leakage but rare disorders remain clinically problematic.

model_io.model: Six classification algorithms (Random Forest, Decision Tree, Linear SVM, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Gradient Boosting, soft-voting Ensemble)
inputs: CBC measurements from 24,545 records (11 blood parameters)

model_io.model: SMOTE oversampling and hyperparameter tuning pipeline

hypotheses.hypothesis: Machine learning algorithms can automatically capture complex CBC patterns for multi-disorder classification beyond conventional interpretation
hypotheses.result: Gradient Boosting and Random Forest achieved 90.1–90.3% accuracy; interpretable outputs consistent with clinical procedures

hypotheses.hypothesis: Red cell distribution width, platelet count, and RBC count are primary discriminative features for hematological diagnosis
hypotheses.result: Identified as most influential predictive features across models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Class imbalance mitigation enables rare disease detection
hypotheses.result: CHIP, hemophilia, and von Willebrand disease remain poorly classified (F1≤0.37) despite SMOTE

title: PBRE-DETR for lightweight colonoscopy polyp detection with boundary residual enhancement
task: Lightweight polyp detection in colonoscopy images with boundary-aware enhancement
key_results: 95.41% mAP50 and 76.05% mAP50–95 on Kvasir-SEG with 13.87M parameters; 6.96 pp improvement in weak-boundary AP75; 49.0 FPS on edge device
comments: Solid performance on benchmark but recall decreased on independent ETIS-LaribPolypDB dataset, suggesting potential generalization limitations.

model_io.model: PBRE-DETR (Polyp Boundary Residual Enhancement Detection Transformer)
CSP/C2f backbone with raw-preserving boundary residual enhancement

outputs: edge inference at 49.0 FPS on Jetson Orin Nano

hypotheses.hypothesis: Boundary residual enhancement specifically improves weak-boundary lesion localization
hypotheses.result: 6.96 pp AP75 gain over baseline; benefit stronger under strict localization criteria

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lightweight architecture maintains high mAP performance across lesion size categories
hypotheses.result: Achieved highest mAP50–95 across small, medium, and large lesion tertiles

title: Fractional order analysis and modeling of Andes orthohantavirus transmission dynamics using a nonsingular fractional derivative
task: Modeling Andes orthohantavirus transmission dynamics with fractional-order differential equations
key_results: Fractional order α=0.92 identified; human-to-human transmission dominant; rapid quarantine substantially suppresses epidemic trajectories
comments: Mathematically rigorous but validation limited to single outbreak; practical utility for prediction requires prospective testing.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fractional-order derivatives capture memory effects in ANDV transmission better than integer-order models
hypotheses.result: α=0.92 calibrated; global stability proven via fractional Lyapunov methods

hypotheses.hypothesis: Human-to-human transmission dominates over rodent-environment spillover in closed outbreaks
hypotheses.result: Identified as dominant driver in 2026 MV Hondius outbreak

title: Efficient Hamiltonian dynamics tomography
task: Efficient reconstruction of local Hamiltonian dynamics from measurement data
key_results: Polynomial sample and computational complexity achieved for Hamiltonian dynamics tomography; enables practical training of Hamiltonian variational circuits and certification with provable efficiency
comments: The scalability breakthrough for quantum process tomography addresses a critical bottleneck in near-term quantum computing, though applicability to realistic noise profiles requires further validation.

model_io.model: Quantum process learning for Hamiltonian dynamics
inputs: measurement data from unknown Hamiltonian evolution

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local Hamiltonian dynamics can be efficiently reconstructed without prohibitive measurement overhead
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; polynomial sample and computational efficiency achieved

hypotheses.hypothesis: Protocol enables scalable variational circuit training and hardware benchmarking
hypotheses.result: Supported; applications demonstrated in quantum machine learning and noise characterization

title: Spectral energy descriptors for QSPR modelling of cervical cancer drugs: a comparative study with degree- and distance-based topological indices
task: Comparative QSPR modeling of cervical cancer drugs using spectral vs. topological descriptors
key_results: Spectral energies and conventional topological indices show marginal performance differences; both fail on crystal-packing properties; Balaban index uniquely retains signal for melting point and refractive index
comments: The finding that spectral descriptors are strongly collinear with molecular size and counting analogues limits their practical advantage, though the reproducible dataset provides value for future pharmaceutical screening studies.

inputs: five spectral energies from adjacency/Laplacian/distance matrices
outputs: predictions of ten physicochemical properties (melting point, refractive index, surface tension, etc.)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spectral descriptors offer superior predictions compared to degree- and distance-based topological indices
hypotheses.result: Rejected; both families perform equivalently except Balaban index retains signal for melting point, refractive index, and surface tension

hypotheses.hypothesis: Size-normalized descriptors better capture molecular properties
hypotheses.result: Supported for melting point, refractive index, and surface tension; both descriptor families fail on crystal-packing-governed properties

title: The emergence and dynamics of cooperation through interpersonal synchrony
task: Agent-based modeling of cooperation emergence mediated by interpersonal synchrony
key_results: Nonlinear relationship between synchrony and cooperation; small-world networks enable cooperation at lower synchrony levels than complete networks; sustained cooperation requires continued synchrony integration, not memory alone
comments: The transient cooperation phase after synchrony removal suggests synchrony acts as a cognitive bootstrap rather than a stable cooperative equilibrium, raising questions about real-world intervention durability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Interpersonal synchrony directly promotes cooperation by increasing perceived cooperation
hypotheses.result: Supported nonlinearly; effect modulated by cooperation barrier, information weights, and network topology

hypotheses.hypothesis: Memory alone sustains cooperation after synchrony removal
hypotheses.result: Rejected; cooperation declines despite high memory weighting, indicating synchrony integration is essential for maintenance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Small-world networks support higher cooperation than complete networks
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; small-world topology exhibits lower synchrony threshold and higher equilibrium cooperation
